label: TP
reason: User-supplied parameter names flow directly into the response body without sanitization. Although 'param' is derived from parameter names checked against a magic string ('BenchmarkTest01427'), an attacker can encode script tags within the parameter name (e.g., ?<script>=BenchmarkTest01427) to reflect XSS. The variable 'bar' receives this tainted 'param' and is printed to the writer (line 73), and X-XSS-Protection is disabled.

evidence.note: Source of taint: request.getParameterNames() populates 'param' with user-controlled parameter names.
Sink entry: 'bar' is assigned 'param', propagating user input to the inner function.
Direct reflection: response.getWriter().println(bar) outputs unsanitized user input to HTML body.
